thereof,

13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                 2
                                             ECOFIN.1.B                                       EN
Whereas:

(1)    The Savings and Investments Union (SIU) strategy is part of the Commission strategy to
       provide a vision of the Union as an economic powerhouse. For that purpose, it is necessary
       to establish a single market for financial services by addressing market inefficiencies
       resulting from fragmentation and to create the truly integrated European capital markets
       which are accessible to all citizens and businesses across the Union. It is also important
       that the financial markets' potential of the Union is unlocked by providing access to more
       efficient capital-market based financing and by facilitating cross-border capital flows,
       which in turn should support the economy of the Union, stimulate job creation and enhance
       competitiveness.

(2)    It is necessary to foster a seamless capital market across the EU by strengthening the
       supervisory framework and addressing regulatory fragmentation, thereby ensuring better
       integration of capital markets throughout the Union. In particular, while the integration of
       capital markets in the Union should ultimately be a market-driven process, certain barriers
       stemming notably from the Union legislative framework can obstruct progress. The Union
       should therefore focus on removing barriers in the sectors of trading, post-trading and asset
       management, and barriers hindering the uptake of new technologies. As market integration
       is deepened, it is also crucial for the Union supervisory framework to evolve in accordance
       with it.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                      3
                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                              EN
(3)    In the context of the political objective of simplifying financial services legislation and
       delivering more effective and efficient implementation of Union policies, the Commission,
       after having consulted the European Supervisory Authorities, AMLA, the Council and the
       European Parliament, sent a letter on 1 October 2025 deprioritising empowerments non-
       essential for the effective functioning of the Level 1 legislations. For those deprioritised
       empowerments where the Commission would be legally required to act (‘shall + a date’)
       legal clarity for stakeholders would be enhanced when the basic act is also amended.

(4)    The development of a deeper and more integrated Union capital market, as envisaged in
       the Savings and Investments Union Communication, requires consistent and effective
       supervision across Member States. Divergent national supervisory practices create legal
       uncertainty, increase the cost of cross-border activity and fragment the single market for
       financial services, thereby hindering market integration and the efficient allocation of
       capital. To address those challenges, it is necessary to strengthen supervisory convergence
       and, where appropriate, entrust the European Securities and Markets Authority (‘ESMA’,
       hereinafter also referred to as 'the Authority') with additional tasks and powers to ensure
       the uniform application of Union law and the effective oversight of entities with significant
       cross-border relevance.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                      4
                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                             EN
(5)    For that purpose, ESMA should be given additional competences and its governance and
       funding framework should be reinforced to promote transparent, accountable and efficient
       decision-making at Union level and to ensure that ESMA has sufficient resources to fulfil
       its expanded responsibilities. The transfer of direct supervisory powers to ESMA in
       relation to significant entities in the field of market infrastructure and ▌ crypto-asset
       services, together with enhanced supervisory convergence tools, should contribute to a
       more integrated, competitive and resilient capital market that delivers better outcomes for
       investors, firms and the broader economy.

(6)    Pursuant to Article 1(2) of Regulation (EU) No 1095/2010 of the European Parliament and
       of the Council(2), ESMA is to act within the powers conferred on it by a range of Union
       legislative acts, including several Directives and Regulations listed therein. To ensure the
       full application of Union financial legislation, ESMA should apply national legislation
       transposing directives in a manner consistent with Union Law in a way that respects the
       primacy of Union Law.

(7)    In addition, Article 1(2) of that Regulation further provides that ESMA is to act within the
       powers conferred by any other legally binding Union act which assigns tasks to ESMA. It
       is necessary to ensure that the scope of ESMA’s responsibilities and tasks automatically
       extends to any subsequent Union legislation conferring powers or functions on ESMA.

(8)    To reflect the progressive extension of ESMA’s direct supervisory, investigatory,
       enforcement and other responsibilities across different sectors of the financial system, it is
       necessary to introduce a definition of financial market participants that are under ESMA’s
       supervision. That definition should encompass all financial market participants for which
       ESMA has been conferred powers. That definition should ensure consistency and clarity in
       the application of ESMA’s supervisory powers, irrespective of the legal instrument from
       which those powers derive, and facilitate the establishment of common procedural and
       organisational arrangements for supervision and enforcement.

(9)    To ensure the effective exercise of its new direct supervisory responsibilities, the
       Authority should establish, under its overall responsibility, structured, transparent and
       proportionate cooperation arrangements with relevant competent authorities and other ▌
       national authorities, Union institutions or Union bodies. Those arrangements should
       apply on an ongoing basis. While the Authority remains solely responsible and
       accountable for the tasks conferred on it, from the date on which the relevant direct-
       supervisory responsibilities are transferred to the Authority, it may need to draw on the
       expertise, supervisory experience and knowledge of national legal, economic,
       organisational and cultural specificities held by relevant competent authorities ▌ . ▌
       Cooperation should therefore enable:




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                        6
                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN
1) the timely exchange of information necessary for (a) the exercise of supervisory tasks and
        (b)the provision, where necessary, of administrative assistance, 2) investigatory or
        enforcement support, 3) participation in on-site activities, 4) liaison functions or 5)
        other operational forms of cooperation.
        The arrangements should be tailored to the sector concerned, while promoting time- and
        resource-efficient supervision. To cater for sectoral specificities, the arrangements should
        also allow ▌ , where appropriate, for different forms of ongoing cooperation, including
        coordinated supervisory teams which should be the default form of cooperation unless
        otherwise agreed, liaison officers or the establishment of local presences of the Authority
        in Member States. Where coordinated supervisory teams are established, the cooperation
        arrangements should, where appropriate, lay down rules on their composition and
        functioning so as to ensure that they operate in an efficient, effective and cost-efficient
        manner, and allow relevant authorities to opt-out. To ensure that those arrangements
        and the forms of cooperation provided for therein remain effective and suited to the
        sector concerned, they should be adopted by the Board of Supervisors on a proposal
        from the Executive Board and be subject to periodic review. Cooperation should be
        guided by the principles of efficiency, proportionality, mutual trust and good faith, and
        should promote the effective use of resources while safeguarding ESMA’s ability to carry
        out its tasks autonomously and consistently, and its sole responsibility for final
        supervisory decisions.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                      7
                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                           EN
(9a)   In order to ensure an orderly transition to the steady state phase laid down in this
       Regulation, it is necessary to provide for sector-specific transitional cooperation
       arrangements between the Authority and the relevant competent authorities. Those
       arrangements should ensure continuity of supervision, legal certainty, the transfer of
       knowledge, documentation and pending supervisory files, and the progressive
       development of the Authority’s operational capacity to perform its tasks autonomously.
       From the date on which the relevant supervisory responsibilities are transferred, the
       Authority should be solely responsible and accountable for the exercise of those
       responsibilities and for the adoption of final supervisory decisions, while being
       supported during a defined, limited period by the relevant competent authorities and
       other national authorities in accordance with approved transition plans. Such
       transitional cooperation should be subject to clear milestones and capacity assessments,
       and should cease once the Authority is operationally ready and, in any event, upon
       expiry of the maximum transition period, including any duly approved extension.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                  8
                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                           EN
(10)   In certain circumstances, temporary exemptions or other transitional arrangements under
       Union financial services legislation may expire before the entry into force or full
       implementation of new or amended provisions introducing a permanent exemption,
       replacement framework, or new regulatory treatment. In addition, significant market
       developments may occur that render compliance with specific requirements under existing
       Union law temporarily disproportionate, operationally impracticable, or unduly
       burdensome in light of prevailing market conditions and the underlying regulatory
       objectives. To ensure legal certainty and regulatory continuity, and to avoid unnecessary
       market disruption, it is appropriate to provide that the no-action letter as set out in Article
       9a of Regulation (EU) No 1095/2010 may also apply in cases where (i) a regulatory
       gap arises during the phasing-in of new requirements, or (ii) exceptional market conditions
       lead to disproportionate compliance burdens for market participants.

(11)   To support cooperation between authorities and facilitate the new collaboration platforms,
       the Authority should develop a corresponding technological platform to facilitate the
       collection, storage, access to and processing of data and information. That data platform
       should contribute to high-quality data governance consistent with FAIR principles
       (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) and also include the supervisory
       technology and other tools to enhance analysis and monitoring capabilities of the relevant
       authorities.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                         9
                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                              EN
(12)   In its capacity as processor of personal data, the Authority should implement appropriate
       technical and organisational measures to ensure the security, availability, maintenance and
       development of the software and IT infrastructure of the platform and that processing of
       personal data in the context of facilitating the access to and exchange of information on the
       platform in ▌ line with Union law laying down the obligations to collect and exchange
       those data and in line with data protection laws. Where the Authority has the obligation to
       processes personal data pursuant to other Union acts, the Authority should fulfil its
       obligations as controllers in regard to that information.

(13)   In view of ESMA’s powers and competence over a broad category of entities and to ensure
       the effective, consistent exercise of its supervisory powers across sectors, it is appropriate
       to rationalise and consolidate in Regulation (EU) No 1095/2010 the procedural framework
       for the exercise of supervisory tools necessary for the Authority to carry out its tasks.
       Those powers, which are currently dispersed across various sectoral Union acts should be
       replaced, to the extent possible, by a single horizontal framework applicable to all entities
       under the Authority’s direct supervision. That horizontal framework should provide a
       coherent set of procedural rules governing ESMA’s requests for information,
       investigations and on-site inspections, as well as the adoption of supervisory measures,
       fines and periodic penalty payments. Such requests for and access to information,
       including during investigations and on-site inspections, may encompass personal data
       insofar as it is relevant and necessary for the performance of the Authority’s tasks, and any
       processing of such data should comply with the applicable Union rules on the protection of
       personal data, in particular the principles of necessity, proportionality and purpose
       limitation.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                    10
                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                              EN
Moreover, that horizontal framework should ensure full respect for the rights of defence and for
        legal professional privilege, and provide for appropriate judicial protection, including the
        review of ESMA’s decisions by the Court of Justice of the European Union. By setting
        such a procedural framework in a coherent and uniform manner and abolishing sector-
        specific procedural provisions, the Union should enhance legal certainty, promote
        supervisory convergence and efficiency, and support the effective and accountable exercise
        of ESMA’s direct supervisory responsibilities. To avoid regulatory overlap or
        inconsistency, to ensure that the Authority exercises its powers in an effective manner, to
        preserve the coherence of the Union acquis and respect the principle whereby specific rules
        take precedence over general rules, where sectoral legislation contains specific provisions
        tailored to the procedural powers of the Authority in particular sectors or areas, those
        provisions should continue to apply and, where appropriate, prevail over the general
        powers laid down in that Regulation.

(14)    Effective supervision and cooperation among competent authorities in the context of cross-
        border provision of financial services is essential to protect investors and foster trust and
        confidence in the financial system within the Union. For that purpose, ESMA should be
        equipped with enhanced supervisory convergence tools, including mechanisms to address
        supervisory failures and tools to facilitate cooperation and resolve disputes between
        competent authorities to ensure that financial market participants are subject to high-
        quality supervision.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                        11
                                            ECOFIN.1.B                                             EN
(15)   To address proven supervisory failures in the approval of financial products, services or
       entities operating across the Union, it is necessary to enable ESMA to require a competent
       authority to seek its opinion, following the process in this Regulation, before granting
       approval where a peer review or an investigation reveals failures in supervision which
       could jeopardize the integrity of financial markets, financial stability, or investor
       protection. The peer review or investigation process, as set out in Article 22(4) of
       Regulation (EU) No 1095/2010, provides a robust and transparent framework for
       identifying supervisory failures and for taking corrective action. ESMA’s opinion should
       provide an additional layer of scrutiny and oversight, ensuring that financial products and
       services, and entities operating in the Union meet the highest standards of supervision. To
       prevent products, services or entities from entering the EU market without adequate
       supervision, it is necessary to enable ESMA to recommend that competent authorities take
       corrective actions to address any shortcomings in supervision identified by ESMA.

(16)   To facilitate regular and structured information exchange, propose solutions, and enhance
       cooperation to address common challenges and risks, and to support the overall goal of
       consistent and effective supervision, it is necessary to provide for collaboration platforms
       between competent authorities. Such platforms should be flexible, enabling ESMA to
       initiate or respond to requests from competent authorities, and should not prejudice the
       existing supervisory mandates and responsibilities of those competent authorities. Those
       collaboration platforms should also promote transparency, accountability, and a culture of
       compliance among financial market participants, with ESMA exercising its powers to
       resolve disputes and ensure compliance with Union law.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                   12
                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                             EN
(17)   Due to the lack of a mechanism for mutual recognition of administrative decisions,
       national competent authorities have significant difficulties in enforcing recovery of
       administrative fines in a cross-border context. To ensure effective enforcement of rules and
       the proper functioning of the single market in the area of financial services, it is necessary
       to introduce a mechanism for mutual recognition of decisions imposing an administrative
       fine and for assistance in executing requests to recover such a fine and such mechanism
       should be based on the principle of mutual trust. To that end, the grounds for a refusal to
       execute the request to recover an administrative fine should be limited to the minimum
       necessary.

(18)   To ensure a consistent and transparent approach to the financing of ESMA’s supervisory
       activities, it is necessary to harmonise and consolidate the principles governing the levying
       of fees on entities under ESMA’s competence, which are currently set out separately in
       sectoral legislation conferring direct supervisory powers on ESMA. Establishing common
       principles on the scope, calculation, and transparency of such fees should promote a level
       playing field among entities across sectors, ensure the proportional application of
       supervisory costs, and provide legal certainty for both existing and new entities falling
       under ESMA’s competence. Those fees should cover all costs incurred by ESMA in the
       performance of its supervisory tasks ▌ . ESMA should be appropriately financed. ▌




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                     13
                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                              EN
(18a)   ESMA should be financed through 60 % Union funds and 40 % Member State
        contributions made in accordance with the weighting of votes set out in Article 3(3) of
        the Protocol (No 36) on transitional provisions for ESMA's tasks that are not fee funded.
        The adjustment of the relative funding shares should not, in itself, lead to a reduction in
        ESMA’s overall co-funded budget, without prejudice to the annual budgetary procedure
        and the multiannual financial framework. Within 12 months of entry into force of this
        Regulation, the Commission should assess whether the existing methodology produces
        proportionate, stable and predictable allocations of contributions among Member States,
        and, if not, propose appropriate legislative revisions to the European Parliament and to
        the Council. Those revisions should balance the collective benefits of integrated and
        resilient Union capital markets with fair reflection of individual Member States’ market
        activity and supervisory responsibilities. The existing methodology should remain in
        effect until any revision enters into force. The Commission should review the applicable
        methodology periodically to ensure indicators remain representative and to evaluate the
        distributional impact across Member States.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                  14
                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN
(18b)   In order to strengthen accountability, transparency and sound financial governance in
        relation to supervisory fees charged by the Authority, a Fees Committee should be
        established. That Committee should support the Board of Supervisors and the Executive
        Board by providing additional internal scrutiny of the methodology, level and evolution
        of supervisory fees and of the related expenditure financed through those fees. In
        particular, it should verify compliance with the cost-recovery principle, assess whether
        fee-financed resources are used efficiently, and consider the impact of fees on different
        categories of supervised entities and across Member States, including smaller entities
        and new market entrants. To ensure balanced representation and appropriate
        supervisory expertise, the Committee should be composed of representatives of national
        competent authorities appointed by the Board of Supervisors on a rotational basis,
        taking into account the relative size of supervised markets, Member States’ contribution
        to the funding of the Authority, and the need to reflect different market sizes and
        supervisory perspectives. The Committee should deliver opinions on the annual and
        multiannual estimates of supervisory fee revenue and related expenditure, as well as on
        the annual fee transparency report, before the adoption or publication of the relevant
        documents. In the interests of transparency, those opinions should be published in an
        annex to the Authority’s annual report and, where the Board of Supervisors departs
        from such an opinion, the reasons for that departure should also be published.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                   15
                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                          EN
(19)   In light of the future new competences of ESMA, its governance structure should be
       adapted accordingly. To ensure the effective and impartial functioning of ESMA it is
       necessary to strengthen its governance by introducing an independent Executive Board
       with full-time members, which should enhance its capacity to take swift and Union-
       oriented decisions, in particular for the supervision of financial market participants. The
       Executive Board, composed of the Chairperson and five independent full-time members
       with diverse supervisory experiences and expertise in the sectors under ESMA’s
       supervision, should be responsible for decisions addressed to financial market participants
       in supervisory matters. The Executive Board should also be responsible for initiating
       procedures and preparing reasoned recommendations for decisions by the Board of
       Supervisors addressed to one or a limited number of competent authorities, including
       dispute settlements and breaches of Union law. In the case of peer reviews, the Executive
       Board shall give an opinion on the draft report of the peer review committee. The
       Executive Board’s involvement in preparing these decisions is intended to increase the
       consistency of the decision-making and to ensure that the decisions take into account a
       common European interest. The Executive Board should also assume the competence of
       the current Management Board in preparing ESMA’s work programmes and budget. This
       should ensure effective, impartial and EU-oriented decisions. To ensure transparency and
       democratic control, the full-time members of the Executive Board should be appointed by
       the Council, based on a shortlist drawn up by the Commission with the assistance of the
       Board of Supervisors, following approval by the European Parliament.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                     16
                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                           EN
(20)   To ensure a clear division of responsibilities and effective checks and balances, the Board
       of Supervisors should remain ESMA’s main body for regulatory decisions and supervisory
       convergence. To enhance the Union dimension in the decision-making process within the
       Board of Supervisors, its composition should be adjusted to include the full-time members
       of the Executive Board as non-voting members ▌ . To ensure a balanced approach and the
       consideration of national perspectives, the Board of Supervisors should have the power to
       object to major supervisory decisions taken by the Executive Board within 10 days (or 24
       hours in urgent cases). To ensure proper information sharing between the two Boards,
       the Executive Board should be required to forward draft decisions to the Board of
       Supervisors in a timely manner, report to the Board of Supervisors twice a year on its
       supervisory activities and should be able to request opinions on supervisory matters.

(21)   It is necessary to streamline and align the review clause of the Regulation (EU)
       No 1095/2010 with existing evaluation requirements for the agencies, as set out in the Joint
       Statement and Common Approach on EU decentralised agencies from July 2012, which
       provide for periodic evaluations every five years instead of three years. The targeted
       reviews provided for in that Regulation, starting five years after the date of entry into
       force, replace evaluations and enable the Commission to assess the relevant aspects of
       ESMA's performance after an adequate period of time has elapsed. This approach is
       consistent with the objective of reducing regulatory burdens and promoting a more targeted
       and effective regulatory framework, allowing for informed decisions on potential
       simplifications and improvements.

                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                              EN
(22)    Central counterparties (‘CCPs’) within the Union are currently authorised and supervised
        by the competent authorities of the Member States in which they are established, in
        cooperation with ESMA and CCP colleges. Despite progress achieved so far in
        harmonising supervisory activity for CCPs in the Union, diverging supervisory practices
        for CCPs amongst those national authorities across the Union persist, creating an unlevel
        playing field among CCPs within the Union. This increases the complexity of the Union
        CCP framework and places an additional burden and additional costs on CCPs within the
        Union, including when compared with Tier 2 CCPs directly supervised by ESMA. With
        the development of deeper, more liquid Union capital markets under the Savings and
        Investments Union, that unlevel playing field could increase the risk of, and incentives for,
        supervisory arbitrage which could in turn lead to financial stability issues. Therefore, ▌ to
        ensure that the prudential, organisational and business conduct requirements for CCPs
        within the Union are applied in a uniform manner, in particular for CCPs with substantial
        clearing activity, CCPs with a material cross-border dimension, and CCPs that are part of a
        group that includes other Union CCPs or Tier 2 CCPs, should be supervised by ESMA,
        based on its expertise and experience in the application of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of
        the European Parliament and of the Council3. CCPs with low clearing activity and a more
        domestic standing, deemed less significant, should continue to benefit from the supervision
        of local authorities with a greater familiarity with domestic markets. ▌




3      Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 4 July 2012
       on OTC derivatives, central counterparties and trade repositories (OJ L 201, 27.7.2012, p. 1,
       ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2012/648/oj).

(23)    To determine which CCPs authorised under Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 should be
        deemed significant and thus subject to supervision by ESMA, it is necessary to provide
        clear and objective criteria, which should reflect the activities and risks of the CCPs
        concerned. With the aim of simplification and of avoiding unnecessary administrative
        burden, an existing CCP determined as significant at a later stage, should not be re-
        authorised.

(24)    National competent authorities supervising less significant CCPs should have stronger
        cooperation with ESMA to ensure a consistent approach to supervision and hence ensure a
        level playing field for CCPs. In case they wish to do so, Member States should have the
        option to designate ESMA as the competent authority for less significant CCPs established
        in their jurisdictions. Moreover, should a previously significant CCP no longer meet the
        conditions to be considered as such, a sufficient transition period should be granted to the
        national competent authority to allow it to prepare before formally taking over supervisory
        responsibilities for that CCP. Alternatively, the Member State should be able to leave the
        supervision of this previously significant CCP to ESMA. In addition, to ensure consistency
        and a level playing field between significant and less significant CCPs, ESMA should also
        be the authority responsible for authorising interoperability arrangements and for co-
        chairing the colleges for less significant CCPs. The new supervisory arrangements for
        CCPs in the Union, in particular the role of ESMA as competent authority for significant
        CCPs, should be reflected in Regulation (EU) 2021/23 of the European Parliament and of
        the Council5▌

(25)   ESMA should closely cooperate with, and draw on the experience of, the bodies
       responsible for the oversight of CCPs authorised in the Union and with authorities
       experienced in the supervision of CCPs to benefit from the knowledge of those bodies. For
       that purpose, ESMA should develop comprehensive cooperation arrangements with those
       bodies and authorities, including the national competent authority in the Member State in
       which the CCP concerned is established, the European Central Bank, other central banks of
       issue of ▌ Union currencies that the CCP processes, the competent authorities responsible
       for the supervision of the trading venues and the central securities depositories served by
       the CCP, and the competent authority responsible for the supervision of the most active
       clearing members. Those arrangements should set out the specific modalities and
       operational arrangements both in ongoing supervision and in exceptional circumstances,
       such as emergency situations.

                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN
(26)   The new supervisory responsibilities granted to ESMA and the changes to ESMA’s
       internal organisational structure, including the removal of the CCP Supervisory
       Committee, whose tasks should be assigned to the newly established Executive Board,
       should be reflected in Regulation (EU) No 648/2012. Due to the unique status of third-
       country CCPs, the provisions concerning the procedures applying to them should remain in
       Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 rather than shifting those provisions to Regulation (EU)
       No 1095/2010. Furthermore, taking into account those changes, to further simplify the
       future organisational structure and working arrangements, and to remove unnecessary
       burden, significant CCPs should not be required to have a college. When developing
       comprehensive cooperation arrangements with other authorities, ESMA should take due
       consideration of the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures
       (PFMI). Similarly, given ESMA’s new supervisory responsibilities for significant CCPs,
       the requirements for ESMA opinions in relation to those CCPs should be removed.
       Supervisory arrangements for less significant CCPs should largely remain as they were, as
       those CCPs have a more domestic scope and should benefit from the local knowledge and
       expertise of national authorities.

                                            ECOFIN.1.B                                         EN
(27)    Regulation (EU) 2024/791 of the European Parliament and of the Council6 amended
        Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council7 to remove
        obstacles to the emergence of consolidated tapes in bonds, shares and exchange-traded
        funds ('ETFs') and OTC derivatives. For a given share or ETF at any given timestamp, the
        provider of the consolidated tape is required to disseminate the European best bid and offer
        price (‘EBBO’) and the volume available at those prices across the Union. However, the
        consolidated tape would not disclose the identity of the trading venue of the EBBO, as it
        would not attribute the volumes that are available at the EBBO to individual trading
        venues, nor would it include bid and offer data beyond the EBBO and accompanying
        volumes. That significantly limits the value added of the consolidated tape, depriving its
        users of the ability to locate the volumes available at the EBBO and of a representative
        view of the depth of liquidity that is available for trading. Therefore, to further enhance its
        attractiveness, the consolidated tape for shares and ETFs should offer a more in-depth view
        of trading interests, covering the three best buying and selling prices, with the volumes
        available at those prices, and the indication of the individual trading venue on which those
        volumes are available.

30)    The organisational requirements laid down in Article 19(3) and in Article 47 of Directive
       2014/65/EU do not take into account whether a market operator or an investment firm
       operating a trading venue is part of a group. In particular, any intra-group arrangement for
       resource or function allocation between group entities is treated in the same way as an
       outsourcing arrangement entered into with entities outside the group. That approach fails to
       acknowledge the emergence of cross-border groups of trading venues and, as a result,
       limits the ability of those groups to enjoy group synergies and benefit from economies of
       scale, thus creating barriers to the cross-border allocation of resources and functions within
       a group. Additionally, allocating resources within a group, where all entities are subject to
       the same internal controls and procedures, carries a lower level of risk compared to
       outsourcing to external parties. The current approach, however, does not sufficiently
       distinguish between the risks associated with intragroup resource allocation and external
       outsourcing. Therefore, organisational requirements for trading venues should be
       simplified for trading venues that are part of a group and that intend to rely on the
       resources of or the performance of a function by another entity that is part of the same
       group and that is located in the Union. Such group arrangements should not be considered
       outsourcing for the purpose of Regulation No (EU) 600/2014, provided that certain
       conditions are met to ensure effective supervision. A trading venue that relies on the
       resources of or the performance of a function by another entity that is part of the same
       group should however remain fully responsible for the discharge of its obligations under
       Regulation No (EU) 600/2014. Given the increased supervisory risks, an intra-
       group arrangement that involves an entity located outside the Union should still be
       considered outsourcing.

(40)    ▌ On 20 March 2025 ▌ , the European Council adopted conclusions where it called for the
        improvement of the efficiency of supervision of Union capital markets and the reduction of
        their fragmentation. Furthermore, the Draghi and Letta reports ▌ called for a more
        integrated supervision at the Union level. Pursuant to Title VI of Directive 2014/65/EU,
        national competent authorities are currently responsible for the oversight of trading
        venues in the Union. The current framework of national supervision of trading venues
        has given rise to material divergences in the manner in which the requirements laid
        down in Union legislation are interpreted and applied by competent authorities across
        Member States. Those divergences increase compliance costs for operators active on a
        cross-border basis and reduce legal certainty for those operators as regards the
        regulatory treatment of their activities. In consequence, they create an unlevel playing
        field, impede the effective exercise of fundamental freedoms in the Treaties and
        undermine the smooth functioning of the single market for financial services. Further
        harmonisation of rules alone does not constitute an adequate remedy, given that
        legislation, by its nature, cannot exhaustively prescribe every detail required to ensure
        uniform supervisory outcomes under all circumstances. It also undermines the objective
        of simplifying the EU rulebook.

                                            ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN

(40a)   To ensure that the transfer of supervisory competences to ESMA is proportionate insofar
        as it is limited to those cases where centralised supervision is necessary to ensure the

       local agents and differing national deadlines. Those divergences hinder the functioning of
       the internal market, as UCITS and AIFs must navigate a patchwork of national rules and
       processes when operating in several Member States. It is therefore necessary to streamline
       marketing notification and de-notification procedures, shorten processing times and
       remove national requirements that create obstacles to the cross-border marketing of
       investment funds. For that purpose, Regulation (EU) 2019/1156 is amended to allow
       UCITS and AIFMs ▌ to notify their home Member State of their intention to market units
       or shares of UCITS or AIFs in other Member States through a simplified procedure. ▌

(68)   As part of its authorisation, where a UCITS intends to market its units in a Member State
       other than its home Member State, a UCITS should enclose with its application, inter
       alia, its fund rules or instruments of incorporation, its prospectus and, where
       appropriate, its latest annual report, and its key information documents, translated in
       accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014, and the other required documents at
       least in a language customary in the sphere of international finance. The UCITS should
       provide information on the appointment of inter alia the management company and the
       depositary. In the event of any foreseen material changes to the documentation and
       information submitted to the competent authorities of the UCITS home Member State
       subsequent to the application for the initial authorisation, such changes should be
       notified in advance.

For the purposes of this Regulation only, "material change" means a change to information or
        documentation previously submitted that by reason of its nature, scale or effects, could
        reasonably be expected to influence an investor’s decision to acquire, hold, redeem or
        dispose of units or shares in a fund, affect compliance with this Regulation, affect the
        rights or interests of investors or cause the information or documentation previously
        submitted to be inaccurate, incomplete or misleading. The launch of a new share class
        previously disclosed in offering documents shall not qualify as a material change. These
        changes may relate to the governing body of the UCITS (where applicable) or to an
        existing relationship with a statutorily provided service provider, namely the
        management company, including change of status as externally managed or vice versa,
        or the depositary or the statutory auditor. Such changes may also be related to third-
        party delegates and relevant entrusted tasks, in particular cross-border distribution
        arrangements. They may further relate to legal and commercial aspects of the UCITS
        and its offering, such as changes to the terms regarding issue, sale or redemption, the
        investment objective and policy of the UCITS, changes to legal form and structuring as
        well as corporate action related events, e.g. a merger. It is important that the
        notification of material changes does not create unnecessary barriers in terms of time
        and costs to market a UCITS, noting the broader objective to improve and simplify
        access to the Single Market. Similarly, this would apply to AIFMs, EUVECA managers,
        EuSEF managers.

       the effective functioning of the internal market and the consistent enforcement of
       Regulation (EU) 2023/1114.

(95)   National competent authorities ▌ should continue to exercise supervisory responsibilities
       for non significant crypto-asset service providers and ▌ should cooperate closely with
       ESMA in accordance with this Regulation. To ensure consistent application of this
       Regulation across the Union, ESMA should possess sufficient powers under Regulation
       (EU) No 1095/2010 and this Regulation. ESMA should develop technical standards
       where mandated to do so, issue guidelines, conduct peer reviews and coordinate
       investigations where necessary. In emergency situations, ESMA may adopt product
       intervention measures and issue binding decisions to national competent authorities or
       directly to CASPs. These powers should enable ESMA to prevent regulatory arbitrage
       and safeguard consumer protection, market integrity and financial stability without
       assuming direct supervision of non-significant CASPs.

(96)   Certain firms subject to Union legislative acts on financial services are already allowed
       to provide all or some crypto-asset services without being required to obtain an
       authorisation as a crypto-asset service provider under Regulation (EU) 2023/1114.
       These entities should continue to be supervised for their crypto-assets activities by the
       competent authorities that granted them authorisation under other Union acts. However,
       the national competent authorities should cooperate with ESMA to ensure enhanced
       supervisory convergence and that the provision of crypto-asset services by these entities
       does not pose a threat to market integrity.

(97)   To supervise significant crypto-asset service providers, ESMA should have the powers to
       suspend or, prohibit the provision of a crypto-asset service, to withdraw the authorisation
       of a crypto-asset service provider, to investigate infringements of the rules on market

       supervisory measures and to impose fines. When determining the type and level of an
       administrative penalty or other administrative measure, ESMA should take into account all
       relevant circumstances, including the gravity and the duration of the infringement and
       whether it was committed intentionally. In order to carry out its supervisory duties, ESMA
       should cooperate and be assisted by other competent authorities as well as the competent
       authorities responsible for the supervision of ▌ Directive (EU) 2015/849 ▌ .

       Duty of cooperation ▌

       1.    The Authority shall carry out its tasks in cooperation with relevant competent

             exercise their tasks. When exercising its tasks, the Authority may draw from the

                   Authority’s attention and request supervisory consideration; and

            (j)    they shall specify cooperation in emergency situations, including with central
                   banks, resolution authorities and other authorities responsible for crisis
                   management, financial stability, security or preparedness, as well as in
                   relation to Regulation (EU) No 2022/2554 responsibilities.

       6.   The practical arrangements for cooperation shall be approved by the Board of
            Supervisors, based on a proposal from the Executive Board. The Board of
            Supervisors may require amendments where appropriate before approving those
            arrangements. The Executive Board ▌ and the authorities shall ensure their timely
            and effective implementation.

            The authorities shall, in cases where the Authority is exercising direct supervisory
            tasks, follow the instructions given by the Executive Board when performing the
            tasks assigned to them under the cooperation arrangements.

       7.   The practical arrangements for cooperation established pursuant to this Article shall
            be subject to periodic review by the Authority, in consultation with the authorities, to
            ensure their continued effectiveness, proportionality and consistency with the
            Authority’s evolving supervisory capacity and Union law. The Board of Supervisors
            may request the Executive Board to propose amendments where experience
            demonstrates that an arrangement is not operating effectively or proportionately.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                 104
                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN
       Article 8b
       Cooperation during the transition period

       1.   During a preparation phase running between the date of entry into force of the
            amending regulation and the date on which the responsibility for the direct
            supervisory mandates is transferred to ESMA according to this Regulation and the
            relevant sectororal Regulations, ESMA and the relevant national authorities shall
            closely cooperate and prepare the transfer of powers to ESMA.

            This Article does not apply to sectors or subsectors subject to direct supervision by
            ESMA prior to [date of this Regulation taking effect].

       2.   To ensure continuity of supervisory tasks, the orderly transfer of supervisory
            responsibilities, knowledge and documentation and to support the development of
            the Authority’s supervisory capacity, the Authority and relevant national
            authorities shall establish sector specific transitional cooperation arrangements for
            the purpose of carrying out tasks according to Article 8(1), point (l) during a
            transition period.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                              105
                                         ECOFIN.1.B                                           EN
       3.   The transition period shall commence on the date on which the relevant direct-
            supervisory responsibilities are transferred to the Authority. From that date, the
            Authority shall be the responsible supervisor and shall remain responsible and
            accountable for the exercise of those responsibilities and for all final supervisory
            decisions. During the transition period, the relevant competent authorities and
            other national authorities shall support the Authority in exercising its supervisory
            tasks in accordance with the approved transition plan, including by contributing to
            supervisory activities and to the preparation of supervisory assessments and
            proposed decisions, with a view to developing the Authority’s capacity to perform
            its tasks independently. The Authority shall independently assess and validate any
            work prepared by a participating authority before relying on it in a supervisory
            decision.

       4.   For significant crypto-asset service providers, the transition period shall end no
            later than two years after the transfer date, unless extended in accordance with
            paragraph 5. For significant trading venues and Pan-European Market
            Operators, central securities depositories and central counterparties, the transition
            period shall end no later than three years after the transfer date, unless extended
            in accordance with paragraph 5.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                 106
                                         ECOFIN.1.B                                           EN
            Before the transitional period expires, the Executive Board shall submit to the
            Board of Supervisors a reasoned assessment, prepared after consulting the
            relevant authorities, of whether the Authority possesses the staff, expertise,
            systems, information and operational capacity necessary to perform its tasks
            effectively and of the permanent structured cooperation model appropriate for
            each sector. The transition period shall end on the date specified in the relevant
            cooperation arrangements, and in any event no later than two or three years after
            the transfer date, as applicable. The Board of Supervisors may, on a reasoned
            proposal from the Executive Board and after consulting the relevant authorities,
            determine that the permanent cooperation arrangements should apply before the
            expiry of the relevant period.

       5.   For a sector subject to a transition period referred to in paragraph 4, where the
            Executive Board concludes that the Authority is not yet operationally ready, it may
            prepare a reasoned request for one extension of no more than 12 months. The
            request shall identify the outstanding deficiencies, the additional support required
            and revised measures and milestones necessary to address those deficiencies. The
            Executive Board shall notify the Board of Supervisors of its intention to request an
            extension and shall submit the reasoned request to the Commission for final
            approval. The extension shall take effect only following approval by the
            Commission in accordance with the applicable procedure.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                 107
                                         ECOFIN.1.B                                           EN
            No further extension shall be permitted. At the end of the applicable transition
            period or, where an extension has been approved, at the end of that extension, the
            transitional cooperation arrangements shall cease to apply and the cooperation
            framework under Article 8a shall apply.

            The Executive Board shall submit the ongoing cooperation arrangements referred
            to in Article 8a to the Board of Supervisors sufficiently in advance of the end of the
            transition period. A failure to approve those arrangements shall not constitute
            grounds for extending the transition period. Pending approval of the ongoing
            cooperation arrangements referred to in Article 8a, the Authority and the relevant
            national authorities shall cooperate in accordance with Article 8a(2) and the
            applicable provisions of the sectoral Union acts referred to in Article 1(2).

       6.   The specific provisions covering the transition phase in the cooperation
            arrangements are without prejudice to the Authority’s responsibilities as laid down
            in this Regulation and relevant sector Regulation. The cooperation arrangements
            during the transition phase shall ensure that the Authority develops and maintains
            the necessary capacity to perform its tasks autonomously.

       7.   The specific provisions covering the preparation and transition periods in the
            cooperation arrangements shall be sector specific, where appropriate, and shall, in
            particular, lay down the following:




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                               108
                                         ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN
            (a)    The modalities of the transfer of responsibility for the supervision of the
                   entities that are to become directly supervised by the Authority, including
                   timelines, the transfer of relevant data, pending procedures, supervisory
                   records, investigation files and working documents, the planning of
                   supervisory activities, investigations and on-site inspections, resource and
                   staffing estimates, consultation procedures, sector-specific milestones and
                   criteria for assessing the development of the Authority’s supervisory
                   capacity;

            (b)    the set-up and functioning of Joint Transition Teams, led by a designated
                   Authority staff member, and how relevant activities, information and
                   expertise will transfer into the ongoing cooperation model or models under
                   Article 8a;

            (c)    the modalities for the reimbursement by the Authority of any reasonable,
                   direct and indirect costs incurred by national competent authorities,
                   including resource forecasts, eligible costs, supporting evidence, advance
                   financing where justified, the calculation, invoicing and dispute resolution
                   mechanisms;




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                  109
                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                             EN
             (d)   reciprocal information sharing, treatment of material risks, cooperation with
                   central banks and resolution authorities, Regulation (EU) No 2022/2554
                   responsibilities and emergency or crisis arrangements;

             (e)   an obligation for the Authority to provide, on a semi-annual basis, estimates
                   of the resource needs expected from the national competent authorities

                   The Executive Board shall prepare the specific provisions referred to in this
                   paragraph in consultation with the relevant authorities. The Board of

                   require amendments before approving them.’

            persists after the period for implementing the remedial action plan has expired, the
            Executive Board may submit to the Board of Supervisors a reasoned
            recommendation proposing the entity to suspend, in whole or in part, the relevant
            cross-border services or activities. The recommendation shall demonstrate that:

            (a)    the conditions in paragraph 1 are met;




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                              128
                                        ECOFIN.1.B                                           EN
            (b)    the procedural steps laid down in paragraphs 2 and 3 have been completed
                   and the remediation period has expired without the infringement having
                   been brought to an end or the resulting risks having been adequately
                   mitigated;

            (c)    the suspension is necessary and proportionate, and the risk cannot be
                   adequately addressed by less intrusive means; and

            (d)    the suspension is not likely to have effects on customers or consumers, the
                   orderly functioning and integrity of financial markets or financial stability
                   that are disproportionate to its benefits.

            (e)    The recommendation shall further specify the proposed scope and duration
                   of the suspension. The competent authority shall be given an opportunity to
                   submit final observations.

       5.   The Board of Supervisors may adopt by simple majority a decision requiring the
            suspension of the entity’s activities. The representative of the competent authority
            concerned may participate in the discussion and present its position but shall not
            vote. The decision shall state the reasons on which it is based and specify the
            infringement, the corrective outcome required, the services or activities and
            Member States concerned, and the duration of the suspension.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                               129
                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                          EN
       6.   A suspension under paragraph 5 shall be temporary, targeted and limited to the
            period necessary to address the infringement and the risk giving rise to it. Its initial
            period of application shall not exceed three months. The Board of Supervisors may
            renew the decision for successive periods, each not exceeding three months, on the
            basis of a reasoned assessment prepared by the Executive Board. Each renewal
            shall be subject to a determination by the Board of Supervisors that the conditions
            for the decision continue to be met and that its renewal remains necessary and
            proportionate if the Board of Supervisors is satisfied conditions in paragraph 1
            continue to be met.

            If the suspension is not renewed before its expiry, it shall cease to apply. The
            Board of Supervisors shall lift or narrow the suspension without undue delay
            where those conditions in paragraph 4 are no longer met.

       7.   The decision referred to in paragraph 5 shall be addressed to the competent
            authority, which shall notify the entity and implement the measures necessary to
            give effect to decision of ESMA under applicable Union and national law. The
            Authority shall simultaneously notify the relevant host competent authorities of its
            decision. The host competent authority shall take, within their respective powers,
            the measures necessary to support its application in their territories.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                130
                                         ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN
       7a.   The entity or its competent authority may at any time request that the suspension
             be lifted or narrowed where the infringement has been effectively and sustainably
             remedied, the risk has materially reduced, there has been a material change in
             circumstances, or continuation of the suspension is no longer necessary or
             proportionate. The entity may submit such a request through its competent
             authority, together with the supporting information. The competent authority shall
             transmit the request without undue delay, together with its assessment.

             The Executive Board shall assess the request within 5 working days of receiving
             the information necessary to complete its assessment and shall submit a reasoned
             recommendation to the Board of Supervisors. The Board of Supervisors shall lift
             or narrow the suspension, where the conditions in paragraph 4 are no longer met.
             It may also do so on its own initiative after consulting the Executive Board and the
             relevant competent authorities. The competent authority shall notify the entity of
             the decision. The entity may resume the services or activities to the extent specified
             in that notification.

       7b.   For the purposes of this Article, the Authority may address a duly justified and
             reasoned request for information to any competent authority or other relevant
             person. Any request for information from, and all other engagement with or
             notification to an entity that remains under national supervision shall take place
             through its competent authority. The competent authority shall transmit the

             transmission solely because it disagrees with them.

       ‘Article 28a

       Mutual assistance between competent authorities

       1.   Member States, through the competent authorities, shall assist each other in
            recovering administrative fines imposed for the breach of any provision laid down in
            the acts referred to in Article 1(2), when the administrative fine must be recovered
            within the jurisdiction of a Member State other than the Member State where that
            fine was issued.
            This Article and Article 28b apply mutatis mutandis to the recovery of amounts due
            on the basis of settlements and of periodic penalty payments.
            The decision of the competent authority imposing an administrative fine shall be
            enforceable in all Member States.

       2.   When the decision imposing the administrative fine on the concerned natural or legal
            person in the Member State of the applicant authority has become final and
            enforceable and the fine has not been paid, the requested authority shall, upon
            request of the applicant authority, assist in the recovery of the related amounts in its
            own jurisdiction.
            If the competent authority is not itself, under its national law, tasked with
            recovering the administrative fines, it shall transfer all requests for assistance to
            the authority in its Member State responsible for such recovery.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                  139
                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN
       3.   The request referred to in paragraph 2 shall be transmitted to the requested authority
            by means of a uniform instrument in digital form, which shall contain all the
            following elements:

            (a)    the name, address and other contact details of the requested authority;

            (b)    the name, known address of the addressee of the decision imposing the
                   administrative fine, and any other relevant information for the identification of
                   the addressee;

            (c)    a summary of the relevant facts and circumstances leading to the adoption of
                   the decision imposing the administrative fine;

            (d)    a summary of the decision imposing the administrative fine and a copy thereof;

            (e)    information about the enforceability of the decision and the date when the
                   decision became final and enforceable;

            (f)    the amount of the fine to be paid, including interest and costs, if any;

            (g)    the period within which enforcement should be carried out, such as statutory
                   deadlines or limitation periods;




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                 140
                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN
            (h)    if available, information showing the reasonable efforts made by the applicant
                   authority to enforce the decision in its own jurisdiction, including the
                   ascertained absence of sufficient assets belonging to the concerned natural or
                   legal person thereto to enable the enforcement of the administrative fine;

            (i)    information according to which the concerned natural or legal person has ▌
                   assets in the Member State of the requested authority to enable the enforcement
                   of the administrative fine.

       4.   The applicant authority shall send the digital form and, where required under the
            national law of the Member State of the requested authority, the decision imposing
            the administrative fine to the requested authority translated into the official
            language, or in one of the official languages, of the Member State of the requested
            authority, unless the requested authority and the applicant authority agree that the
            digital form may be provided in another language.

            The decision imposing the administrative fine, accompanied, where required under
            the national law of the Member State of the requested authority, with a translation of
            the decision to impose the fine into the official language, or into one of the official
            languages, of the Member State of the requested authority, unless the requested
            authority and applicant authority agree that such translation may be provided in a
            different language.

                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN
            Article 28b

            General principles applicable to the enforcement of decisions imposing
            administrative fines

       1.   The uniform digital instrument permitting enforcement by the requested authority
            shall constitute the sole legal basis for the enforcement measures taken or initiated
            by the requested authority, in accordance with paragraphs 3 and 4 of Article 28a. It
            shall not be subject to any act of recognition, supplementing or replacement in the
            Member State of the requested authority. It shall constitute the sole legal basis for
            the enforcement measures taken by the requested authority without any further
            formality, supplement or replacement being required. The requested authority shall,
            upon receipt, forthwith take all the necessary measures for the enforcement of the
            sanctioning decision issued by the applicant authority according to the rules and
            procedures laid down by its national law, unless the requested authority invokes
            paragraph 4. The requested authority shall inform the applicant authority with due
            diligence of any action it has taken on the request for recovery.

       2.   The amount recovered from enforcing the decision to impose the administrative fine
            shall accrue to the Member State of the applicant authority in its own currency,
            unless otherwise agreed between the Member State of the applicant authority and the
            Member State of the requested authority. The requested authority shall, if necessary
            for the recovery, convert the administrative fine into the currency of its Member
            State at at a foreign exchange benchmark rate that complies with Regulation (EU)
            2016/1011 and applies on the date on which the administrative fine was imposed.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                142
                                         ECOFIN.1.B                                             EN
       3.   The requested authority may recover the full costs incurred in relation to actions
            taken as referred to in paragraph 1 from the fine it has collected on behalf of the
            applicant authority, including translation, labour and administrative costs,
            irrespective of the outcome of the recovery proceedings.
            If the requested authority is unsuccessful in recovering the fine or periodic penalty
            payment, it may request the applicant authority to bear the costs incurred.

       4.   The requested authority may refuse to enforce the decision of the applicant authority
            to impose an administrative fine only if it has established any of the following:

            (a)    the request does not fulfil all the requirements set out in paragraphs 3 and 4 of
                   Article 28a;

            (b)    the decision is no longer enforceable under the law of the Member State of the
                   requested authority due to lapse of time.

            (c)    the enforcement of the decision would be contrary to the principle of ne bis in
                   idem;

            (d)    there are reasonable grounds showing that the execution of the request would
                   be manifestly contrary to public policy in the Member State in which
                   enforcement is sought.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                  143
                                            ECOFIN.1.B                                            EN
            (da) the estimated costs of the recovery proceedings would be higher than the fine
                   or periodic penalty payment to be recovered.

       5.   Article 28b and paragraphs 1 to 4 of this Article shall not preclude the application of
            the Council Framework Decision 2005/214/JHA(1) bilateral or multilateral
            agreements or arrangements between Member States in so far as such agreements or
            arrangements help simplify or facilitate further the procedures for the enforcement of
            administrative fines falling under the scope of Articles 28a.

       6.   The Authority shall encourage and facilitate the mutual assistance between
            competent authorities in enforcing administrative fines imposed outside their
            jurisdictions in accordance with Article 28a and this Article.

            Where the requested authority refuses to assist the applicant authority in accordance
            with Article 28a and none of the grounds under paragraph 4 of this Article is
            established, Article 17 shall apply.

            In case of disagreements on the application of this Article or Article 28a, the
            Authority may assist the competent authorities in reaching an agreement, if
            appropriate, in accordance with the procedure set out under Article 19.

13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                      154
                                            ECOFIN.1.B                                              EN
       ‘CHAPTER IIa

       POWERS OF THE AUTHORITY OVER FINANCIAL MARKET PARTICIPANTS
       UNDER THE AUTHORITY’S SUPERVISION

       Article 39a

       Scope

       1.   This Chapter shall apply to all financial market participants under the Authority’s
            supervision unless otherwise specified in this Chapter. However, it shall not apply to
            central counterparties recognised under Article 25 of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012.

       2.   If the provisions of this Chapter conflict with a provision of another Union act
            governing specific aspects of procedural powers of the Authority in a specific sector
            or area, the provision of the other Union act shall prevail and shall apply to that
            specific sector or area. The powers conferred on the Authority, its officials or other
            persons authorised by it shall not be used to require the disclosure of information or
            documents which are subject to legal professional privilege.




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                  155
                                          ECOFIN.1.B                                              EN
            Article 39b

            Requests for information

       1.   For the purpose of exercising its tasks, the Authority may request financial market
            participants under the Authority’s supervision, persons involved in the activities of
            financial market participants under the Authority’s supervision or affected by them,
            related third parties, third parties to whom the financial market participants under the
            Authority’s supervision have outsourced operational functions or activities and
            persons otherwise closely and substantially related or connected to the financial
            market participants under the Authority’s supervision or their activities and any other
            persons as provided for in other Union acts, to provide all information necessary in
            order to carry out its duties under this Regulation and other Union acts.

       2.   When sending a simple request for information under paragraph 1, the Authority
            shall refer to this Article as the legal basis for the request, state the purpose of the
            request, specify the information required, ▌ set a time-limit within which the
            information is to be provided and inform about the possible fines in case of incorrect
            or misleading replies.

       3.   When requesting the information under paragraph 1 by a decision, the Authority
            shall:




13779/1/26 REV 1                                                                                       156
                                           ECOFIN.1.B                                              EN
            (a)    refer to this Article as the legal basis for the request;

            (b)    state the purpose of the request;

            (c)    specify the information required;

            (d)    set a time-limit within which the information is to be provided;

            (e)    indicate possible periodic penalty payments for the provision of incomplete
                   information;

            (f)    inform about the possible fines in case of incorrect or misleading replies;

            (g)    inform of the addressees rights of appeal under this Regulation.

       4.   The persons referred to in paragraph 1 or their representatives and, in the case of
            legal persons or associations having no legal personality, the persons authorised to
            represent them by law or by their constitution or mandate, shall supply the
            information requested.

       5.   The Authority shall, without delay, send a copy of the decision referred to in
            paragraph 3 to the relevant competent authority of the Member State where the
            persons referred to in paragraph 1 and who are concerned with the request for
            information are domiciled or established.
